flags.message: Decisive public forward signal outside the provisioned record: the companion Pacific Legal Foundation petition Tedford's Tenancy, LLC v. City of New York (No. 26-110) was distributed for the same 9/28/2026 conference, drew a call for response on Sep 9, and its response is now due Nov 10, 2026 (extension granted Oct 2). I read the Court as handling the pair together; this shaped the timing/relist forecast and a hold-and-GVR route in the grant number. The frozen band `baseline` does not reflect this docket's call for response after waiver or its six cert-stage amicus briefs (sal-v4 keys on relists/CVSG), so the band anchor was adjusted up substantially. No outcome material for this case surfaced; the live 26-107 docket matched the snapshot.

The event declares moment=distribution, but context has null cutoff/cut_kind and snapshot_provenance=as-stored. The supplied October 5 snapshot includes the August 26 response request and September 24 amicus entry after the August 19 first distribution. I used that supplied forward information set and its frozen baseline band/count, not a reconstructed first-distribution cutoff. This forecast should not be interpreted as conditioned solely on information available at first distribution. No disposition was sought or encountered.

Context freezes distribution_count=1 (DISTRIBUTED for Conference of 9/28/2026), but a Court-initiated 'Response Requested' entry on Aug 26 pulled the petition from that conference before it was considered; the BIO is now due Oct 26. The redistribution that must follow the BIO will resolve relist-increment as a rise although it is a first consideration, not a relist. My relist-increment number (0.97) prices that mechanical redistribution, not a relist signal. Separately, the frozen band is `baseline` while the docket shows a CFR after waiver plus three amicus filings (22 states, NSSF, NRA/SAF); sal-v4 does not condition on a CFR, so my P(grant) departs far from the band anchor by design, not by data error.
No provisioned documents folder was found in the record directory, so the petition and QP text were unavailable.

No filed-document directory, petition/QP text, federal response text, or lower-court opinion was provisioned. The snapshot-linked September 25 letter could not be read through two web-open attempts; a date-bounded Fifth Circuit MCP search returned no result. The forecast therefore relies on the docket skeleton and prior-Term baseline; no substantive question is invented and big_case_score is null. No outcome material was encountered.

Decisive forward signal predating the snapshot: the corpus row for No. 26-104, Rhoney v. Barbosa da Cunha (CA2), the government's petition on the same question with the same counsel on both sides, records cert granted 2026-10-01. This petition was not granted with it, so the forecast is a held-case forecast (GVR if the noncitizens prevail in Rhoney, denial otherwise) rather than an ordinary cert forecast. Not outcome material for this docket.

The provisioned snapshot payload was generated 2026-10-02 (sJsonCreationDate) while the Court's 2026-10-05 order list disposed of or relisted most long-conference petitions. The cell may already have moved (denied or relisted) without that being visible in the snapshot. I did not look up the docket's post-snapshot state.

No record/documents/ directory was provisioned for this paid petition, so the questions presented, petition, government brief and the two petitioner letters were not available as text; the forecast rests on the docket entries, the statpack, the corpus row for the companion case, and the Second Circuit en banc order.

context.json freezes distribution_count=1, but the single distribution entry (Aug 12 2026, for the Sep 28 conference) was superseded the same day by a 'Response Requested' entry, and the response is now due Nov 2 2026: the petition has been considered at zero conferences. The relist-increment claim is stated from the frozen count of 1 as the contract requires; a re-distribution once the response arrives is near-certain and is not a relist in the pre-grant-signal sense.

Forward-mode retrieval surfaced two public developments that postdate the petition but predate the snapshot and were decisive for the number: (1) the Fourth Circuit's published Aug 5 2026 decision in TitleMax of South Carolina v. Spicher (No. 25-2027), which applied its own Harper framework and affirmed Younger abstention over the same Pennsylvania enforcement proceeding; (2) the companion petition TitleMax of Virginia v. Spicher (No. 25-1359), read from the supremecourt.gov docket page via a web fetch (CourtListener holds the docket shell but no entries), which shows the same waiver-then-response-requested track, a South Carolina amicus brief, and a response due the same day as this one's. Nothing about this petition's own disposition was found.

The event declares moment=distribution, but the provisioned context has null cutoff and cut_kind with as-stored provenance. The October 5 snapshot includes the August response request and October 2 opposition after the July 29 first-distribution entry. I used this supplied material under the forward-mode rule, not as a replay or a pure first-distribution information set. No Supreme Court outcome was encountered. The very high distribution-increment forecast reflects likely post-response redistribution, not inferred substantive consideration at the September 28 conference. Please preserve this boundary distinction in cohort comparisons.

Forward cell, not mis-provisioned: the Court called for a response on 2026-08-03 after the respondents waived, and the BIO was filed 2026-10-02, so the single distribution the context freezes (the 2026-09-28 conference) was superseded before consideration. The petition will be redistributed after the reply; the relist-increment claim is near-certain for structural reasons rather than as a forecast of Court interest. The provisioned petition text is truncated (139-page PDF, appendix cut), but the petition body itself was complete through its conclusion.

Forecast uses a truncated petition-and-appendix extraction and no BIO. The available appendix ends within the panel opinion at 45a; the reported rehearing dissents and full underlying evidentiary record were not independently available in the portions read. The missing BIO is consistent with the snapshot's October 30 response deadline, not a provisioning error. See reasoning.md for the resulting uncertainty.

Conditioning note, not a defect: the docket shows the Court requested a response on Jul 30 2026 after the City waived, and the petition was pulled from the 9/28/2026 conference pending a BIO now due Oct 30 2026. The frozen context records band=baseline, distribution_count=1 and response_requested=null, so the scored baseline (~5% pooled reached rate for baseline) does not reflect the call-for-response signal. My P(grant)=0.30 adjusts for it; the gap between the two is the CFR, not a disagreement about the band.

documents.json marks petition.txt truncated (286 pages, the petition plus Appendix Volume I). The petition body itself (through the Conclusion) is intact; only appendix material is cut, and no BIO exists yet to provision. No effect on the forecast.

The provisioned 2026-10-05 as-stored snapshot ends with an August 14 proceeding and has internal creation date August 14, 2026. It extends a requested response to September 28, but contains no response filing or later distribution; the document manifest contains only petition/QP text fetched August 13. Apparent freshness/coverage gap: no inference of nonfiling, conference consideration, or denial was drawn. No current disposition was retrieved. Prediction uses the frozen one-distribution baseline and discounts the missing opposition.

The petition's hold request inconsistently describes the Town of Vinton companion petition as filed and forthcoming, citing application number 25-A1099. Companion filing status was not independently established; the forecast treats a lead-case hold/GVR as a possibility, not confirmed docket history.

Forward cell; decisive public signal came from companion dockets rather than this docket: the lead petition on the same question, No. 25-1383 Indian Harbor Ins. Co. v. Town of Vinton (CA5, Skadden, two amici, response requested 2026-07-27, BIO 2026-08-26, reply 2026-09-09), and No. 26-53 Indian Harbor v. One Lakeside Plaza (rescheduled 2026-08-27). The petition in this cell itself asks the Court to hold it for 25-1383. I also read the 2026-10-05 order list and the 2026-10-02 grant announcements: none of 25-1383, 26-53 or 26-2 appears, so the cluster has not been acted on. No outcome of this case surfaced anywhere; the forecast is derived from the cluster's posture, not from any disposition.

The provisioned snapshot (2026-10-05.json) ends at the 2026-08-14 extension order; the live supremecourt.gov docket fetched 2026-10-06 shows the same six entries, so no brief in opposition had been docketed although it was due 2026-09-28, and no redistribution has occurred. Baseline is current, not stale. No BIO text was provisioned (documents.json lists petition and QP only), so the opposition's arguments were read from the lead case's BIO instead.

The 2026-10-05 forward snapshot's last disclosed proceeding is the 2026-08-17 response request, due 2026-09-16, following distribution for the 2026-09-28 conference. No subsequent proceeding or opposition text is provisioned. This is an input-coverage uncertainty, not evidence that a response was omitted, that the case was held, or that it was decided. Forecast uses the frozen one-distribution/no-CVSG state and does not infer an outcome from silence; no current case disposition was sought. Please check response-document and snapshot freshness when maintaining the corpus.

Companion petition: the petition itself asks to be held for Indian Harbor Insurance Co. v. Town of Vinton, No. 25-1383 (corpus docket 73500284, disposition event still open), and the Fifth Circuit decision under review is an unpublished per curiam that simply applies Town of Vinton. This cell's outcome is almost entirely derivative of the lead case (deny together, or hold and GVR after a reversal there), so its score reads as a forecast of No. 25-1383 more than of this docket. The lead case's trajectory (response requested after a waiver, two amicus briefs, BIO and reply filed) was read from its public supremecourt.gov page; no disposition of either petition surfaced.

The event declares moment=distribution, but provisioned context has null cutoff and cut_kind, snapshot_provenance=as-stored, and two distributions. The October 5 snapshot includes the relist for October 9, after the initial September 28 conference. This forecast uses that supplied latest-record information set and frozen elevated band, not an initial-distribution-only baseline. Preserve this distinction in cohort interpretation; no outcome was sought or encountered.

The provisioned petition.txt is truncated (documents.json: truncated=true) at the start of the appendix, so the Fourth Circuit opinion under review was not readable from the record; the petition body itself is complete. Separately, the docket carries three post-BIO filings (reply Sept 9, respondents' supplemental brief Sept 14, petitioner's response Sept 15) that were not provisioned; the Sept 14 brief discloses that the bankruptcy court dismissed the adversary complaint without prejudice on Sept 10, 2026, a vehicle development I fetched from supremecourt.gov and weighed in the forecast.

The docket names a related cross-petition, City of Bossier City v. Hershey, No. 25-1323 (Monell single-incident liability), which the BIO asks the Court to grant while denying this one. It is not an open event in the corpus (open-events grep) and CourtListener's SCOTUS docket search returns nothing for it, so the cell could not tell whether the two petitions were distributed or relisted together. The relist read in this cell is therefore from this docket alone.

The distribution-moment cell carries an as-stored snapshot with null cutoff and cut_kind rather than a demonstrably moment-bounded baseline. Although named 2026-10-05.json, its latest listed proceeding is September 9 and source creation date is September 24; it lists a September 28 conference. I used the frozen one-distribution state, inferred no hold or survival from later silence, and did not seek or encounter this petition's outcome. The reply is docketed but its text is not provisioned.

The frozen distribution_count of 1 counts the Jul 8 distribution for the Sep 28 conference, which the Jul 27 call for a response superseded before the petition was considered. The forthcoming redistribution after the Sep 9 reply will resolve relist-increment as a relist although it is the petition's first real consideration. Also, the sal-v4 band is `baseline` despite the call for a response, so the scored baseline understates this docket's observed signal; noted for the banding feature set, not as an error in this cell.
